decisions: umbrella Amendment M, Ruling 1 and Ruling 3
umbrella Amendment N, Ruling 1 and Ruling 2
what_lands: The second of the fourteen, and the first performed in Amendment L, Ruling 1's whole shape. active_cast/receipt_walk retires: the family's six mechanics declare both halves (six ViewTag.THEORETICAL pair previews and six APPLIED walk halves delivered as HolderPacket, PER_HOLDER, PAIRED), damage._add_item_active_damage stamps pair_preview_of on the row it authors and hands the walk the AuthoredDeclaration under it, interpreters.active_cast.WALK_INTERPRETER registers at (ACTIVE_CAST, RECEIPT_WALK), and survival.transitions.apply_declared_price prices the declaration at the resistance that packet met. The deferral row leaves docs/behavior-frontier.json in the same commit with the reason its surviving compiled-lane twin can no longer share corrected there (R-36).
why_this_slice_is_startable_now: The same family was implemented and reverted on 2026-08-16 (expected-golden-diff-campaign-close-active-cast-retirement.json, gap-ledger row G4): the from-declaration pricing stage priced every declaration at the one effective resistance a fight publishes, while the pair engine re-prices packets it already authored inside a temporary-lethality window, so R-01 row 8 caught mundo_3champ's score moving 3305.0 -> 3427.7. Umbrella Amendment N ruled the three things that stop it recurring, and all three have landed: Ruling 1's per-packet resistance term (319f076), Ruling 2's source-derived census of post-authoring packet mutations, which is green and which Ruling 2 makes a precondition on any further retirement (78df1f8), and Ruling 3's window-armed covering scenarios (45652c5, eb68690).

landed_against.rule: R-17/R-32/D-97 -- no baseline moves inside any semantic commit of this slice. The code lands against the committed baselines plus this allowlist; a re-capture, if the measurement ever asks for one, is the integration agent's own commit.

qualifying_population.rule: R-20's second half. The count is not readable off the pre-change tree by inspection: this slice moves where a number comes from rather than editing a formula, so which leaves can move is a property of which participants hold a declaring owner of the family, and that is a fact about the committed scenario set rather than about the diff. The population is therefore enumerated from committed artifacts -- the committed docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json at 4e017ea, whose own fields are derived from the behaviour catalog and from scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json's scenario subtrees -- before the slice's first src/ edit. Any occurrence outside it is an unexpected one and stops the slice exactly as an over-count would.
qualifying_population.predicate: Every committed coupled scenario that puts a declaring owner of the active_cast family on a participant. The six owners are read live from the behaviour catalog over rule_owners() -- Hextech Gunblade, Hextech Rocketbelt, Profane Hydra, Ravenous Hydra, Stridebreaker, Tiamat -- which is the same family-to-owner join golden_snapshot.receipt_walk_families() makes for the coverage guard, so the population and the guard that admitted these two scenarios cannot disagree about which rosters can see the family.
qualifying_population.method: scripts.receipt_walk_schedule.population_size over each selected scenario subtree of the committed coupled baseline -- the same instrument, and the same conservative bound, the retirement schedule uses for the remaining rows: the whole scenario subtree, because a slice that moves a family's pricing can move any aggregate downstream of it inside that scenario.

pair_engine_population.why: scripts/golden_baseline.json is the one-attacker pair-engine surface, and this slice adds no pair-engine arithmetic: the two stamps it adds pair-side -- pair_preview_of on the family's breakdown row and the row's own declaration on the events under it -- are not leaves that baseline holds, which records each build's sorted breakdown_keys and its total_damage and neither a row's inner fields nor an event. Zero pair-engine golden diffs is therefore a declared population of zero rather than an observation, and a single diff there stops the slice.

qualifying_population.predicted: 0 occurrences inside a population of 2575, and zero is a prediction rather than a hope. The walk's from-declaration price and the pair engine's price are the same real number with the two multiplications associated differently: the pair engine mitigates the raw magnitude and then applies the holder's magic amp, the walk composes the amp pre-mitigation and mitigates once (Amendment M, Ruling 1), so the two agree to within one unit in the last place -- four orders of magnitude below the 0.005 golden equality grades to (R-13). Under Amendment N, Ruling 1 the resistance each side prices at is now the same one too: the declaration carries the resistance its own packet met, restated by every site that re-prices an authored packet, so a windowed packet is priced at the window's figure rather than at the fight's published baseline. A leaf that did move could therefore only move by 0.01, which qualifies under none of R-15's three tests.

why_the_stamping_half_is_performed_here.rule: Amendment L, Ruling 1 requires a retiring family's pair rows to be stamped pair_preview_of and declared THEORETICAL, and says either half alone is worse than neither.
why_the_stamping_half_is_performed_here.measured: damage._add_item_active_damage authors one summed breakdown row per declared active, keyed active_<owner>, with exactly one damage event under it. So this family's pair-row set is not empty, and stamping it is what takes the pair engine's number out of every roster total that held it -- unlike delta_amp, whose three static holder amps author no summed pair row at all and whose stamping half was therefore discharged as an emptiness.
why_the_stamping_half_is_performed_here.what_survives: The event itself, carrying its declaration and awaiting the walk's price. program.build.walk_repriced_mechanics reads the delivery shape off the declaration: a HolderPacket walk half prices this packet, so the pair engine's event is kept and only its number leaves the roster total, while a rider-delivered preview is dropped whole as before.

reason_text_correction.rule: R-36 -- the machine-derived frontier receipt moves with the slice that moves its count.
reason_text_correction.old_reason: both walks consume this family as the pair engine's timed rows -- participant_timeline._pair_run_fight prices the pair and survival/compile.py stages the resulting packets -- so the declaration reaches them through the pair interpreter rather than through one of its own
reason_text_correction.why_it_had_to_change: The two rows shared one reason object and its first two words are 'both walks', which stops being true of the receipt walk on the commit that registers its interpreter. A retired row that left its reason behind for the surviving row would leave the frontier stating, in the tree's own words, the opposite of what the tree does. The surviving row now names the compiled score walk alone and says in its own words that the receipt walk reads the declaration itself.
reason_text_correction.still_shared_by: The eight families whose receipt-walk half is still deferred and whose numbers still arrive as the pair engine's timed rows on both walks. The constant is unedited for them, which is what keeps this a correction rather than a rewrite.

no_baseline_moves: R-32's five baselines are untouched by every commit of this slice. docs/behavior-frontier.json and docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json are machine-derived receipts whose counters this slice moves, so they move with it (R-36); holding them back would make the slice red against a gate it is forbidden to contain.

measured_after.golden: python scripts/golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_baseline.json -- OK: snapshot identical. The declared pair-engine population of 0 held: the two stamps this slice adds pair-side are a row field and an event field, and that baseline records neither.
measured_after.coupled_golden: python scripts/golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json -- OK: snapshot identical. Zero of the 2575 enumerated leaves moved, which is the predicted reading: the walk's from-declaration price and the pair engine's are the same real number associated differently, and under Amendment N, Ruling 1 they are now priced at the same resistance as well.

the_gate_the_population_could_not_bound.why_it_is_recorded: R-01 row 8 is what stopped the first attempt at this family, and it reads a surface no enumerated coupled population contains: the optimizer's own search over the bench builds. It is recorded here beside the population rather than only in the commit body, because a slice whose only evidence is a green count against a population it chose is the shape Amendment L, Ruling 2 refuses.
the_gate_the_population_could_not_bound.measured: bench_coupled_optimizer.py --fixed-work --isolate --json: cassiopeia_3champ 4003.1 / residual 79, cassiopeia_5champ 5010.8 / 19, mundo_3champ 3305.0 / 12, syndra_mandate_3champ 4642.3 / 98 -- every winner and score identical to what campaign-fingerprints.json pins, and identical again with --no-compiled (routing_divergences empty on all four).
the_gate_the_population_could_not_bound.the_scenario_that_moved_before: mundo_3champ, whose locked build holds Stridebreaker and Voltaic Cyclosword. The reverted attempt moved it to 3427.7 because the walk re-priced the active at the fight's published armour while the pair engine had priced it inside a Firmament window. It is unmoved here, which is Amendment N, Ruling 1's per-packet resistance term reaching a packet for the first time: the declaration carries the armour the window put on it, restated by damage._restate_declaration at the re-pricing site.

measured_after.oracle_receipts_owed: None. R-19 owes an investigator per qualifying occurrence (R-15) and there were none, in a population enumerated in advance and non-empty -- 2575 leaves across two rosters that each put a declaring owner of the family on a participant, one of them arming the holder's magic amp on it.
measured_after.what_the_zero_means_and_what_it_does_not: It means the family's numbers are the same numbers, now produced by the walk from the declaration instead of consumed from the pair engine's rows -- which is the property criterion 8 asks for and the whole of what a retirement is supposed to change. It does not mean the pricing is untested: tests/test_survival_kernel.py records what apply_declared_price actually paid on the covering scenarios and asserts it equals the declaration's own price re-computed from the resistances that packet met, so the number is checked against its own arithmetic rather than only against a baseline that did not move.
